prompt:
Reference image 1 shows the skin witch's human form, the kindly old healer. Draw them exactly as in that image.

Seen from behind and to one side. The healer stands hunched with her back to us, her head drooping forward, limp and empty like a sack, arms hanging slack: a long seam has torn open down her spine, and out of it the true form is unfolding, pale wet limbs pushing out and spreading upward. Her face is turned away and not visible.

Setting: a low, torchlit den of rough timber and stone, drying herbs and bone charms hanging from the beams, and a ring of carved northern runes on the floor.

Palette: dark browns, dark greys, black, undyed wool, raw leather, bone-white and antler-grey; nothing dyed.

Characters (draw them exactly like this):
- The skin witch (name OPEN): in human form, a small, kindly old woman, slightly stooped; soft round face with deep smile lines, long grey braids, faded earned tattoo lines on the chin; wearing fur-trimmed undyed wool, a leather apron hung with herb pouches and bone charms. True form: under the skin, a towering chimera of mismatched human and animal parts fused by raw, wet, pale flesh: several human arms of different sizes and skin tones, a goat's leg, a mouth in its chest full of tongues, an extra jaw, a few tentacles, joints bending the wrong way.

Do not draw: bright dyed colours, painted Skyrim-style Nordic decoration, horned helmets, corpse paint, neat, well-made joinery, horns, wings, a demon, pentagrams, masks, a second face, two faces on one head.

Style: Sword-and-sorcery comic art in the spirit of 1970s-80s Conan the Barbarian and Masters of the Universe: bold confident ink outlines, dramatic lighting, saturated flat colours with hard cel shading and halftone-dot shading, pulpy and dramatic. No text, no logos, no speech bubbles.

Composition: a tight crop from the middle of a larger illustration, so the artwork runs off all four edges of the image. Nothing surrounds the art: no border, no white or cream margin, no paper, no frame, no panel outline.

Aftermath of the reveal. On the den floor lies the healer's empty human skin, collapsed and flat like a shed snakeskin: her grey braids, her fur collar and apron still on it, her face slack, deflated and empty-eyed, recognisably her.
